senses.definition: A group of people within hearing; specifically, a large gathering of people listening to or watching a performance, speech, etc.
examples: We joined the audience just as the lights went down.

quotes.text: One saint's day in mid-term a certain newly appointed suffragan-bishop came to the school chapel, and there preached on “The Inner Life.” He at once secured attention by his informal method, and when presently the coughing of Jarvis […] interrupted the sermon, he altogether captivated his audience with a remark about cough lozenges being cheap and easily procurable.
quotes.reference: 1918, W[illiam] B[abington] Maxwell, chapter V, in The Mirror and the Lamp, Indianapolis, Ind.: The Bobbs-Merrill Company, →OCLC, page 26:

quotes.text: My audience to this not-too-easy operation was a small group of Scottish school lasses, who seemed (perhaps naturally) to find the proceedings somewhat mysterious, but at any rate amusing. I wished they would go away, but they didn't, so I had to get on with the job to the accompaniment of a background of giggles!

senses.definition: A widespread or nationwide viewing or listening public, as of a TV or radio network or program.
A formal meeting with a state or religious dignitary.
examples: She managed to get an audience with the Pope.

quotes.text:
Captain Anderson: Sounds like you convinced the Council to give us an audience.
Ambassador Udina: They were not happy about it. Saren's their top agent. They don't like him being accused of treason.

senses.definition: The readership of a book or other written publication.
examples: "Private Eye" has a small but faithful audience.
The opera singer expanded his audience by singing songs from the shows.

senses.definition: (historical) An audiencia (judicial court of the Spanish empire), or the territory administered by it.
